title: GitHub Actions - Azure Authentication
description: Authenticate GitHub Actions with Azure using service principals, OpenID Connect, and workload identity federation.

data.text: To deploy from GitHub Actions to Azure, you need to authenticate securely. The two most common approaches are publishing profiles (simple) and service principals with OpenID Connect (recommended for teams).

cards.title: Publish Profile
cards.description: Download a publishsettings file from the Azure Portal and store it as a GitHub Secret.
cons: Not suitable for automation at scale

cards.title: Service Principal + Secret
cards.description: Create an Azure service principal with az ad sp create-for-rbac and store the secret as a GitHub Secret.
cons: Secret can expire and needs rotation

cards.title: OpenID Connect (OIDC)
cards.description: Use federated credentials to authenticate without secrets. GitHub exchanges a short-lived OIDC token for an Azure access token.

data.title: Azure CLI - Create a Service Principal
data.content: Create a service principal for GitHub Actions with Contributor role.
data.code:
az ad sp create-for-rbac --name "github-actions-sp" --role Contributor --scopes /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 --sdk-auth

# Output is a JSON object - store each value in GitHub Secrets:
# AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET

data.title: YAML - Authenticate with azure/login
data.content: Use the azure/login action with service principal secrets.

data.title: YAML - Authenticate with OpenID Connect (OIDC)
data.content: Use federated credentials for passwordless authentication.
data.code:
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Login to Azure via OIDC
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
          federated-credential-parameters: |
            audience: api://AzureADTokenExchange
            issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/${{ github.repository_id }}
            subject: repo:myorg/myapp:environment:production

data.title: Use OIDC When Possible
data.text: OpenID Connect removes the need for long-lived secrets. Microsoft recommends OIDC for all production workflows. You configure federated credentials in the Azure AD app registration.

data.title: Exercise: Set Up OIDC Authentication
data.description: Configure GitHub Actions to authenticate to Azure without secrets.
steps: In Azure AD, create an App Registration for GitHub Actions
Add a federated credential with the audience api://AzureADTokenExchange
Assign the appropriate RBAC role to the app registration
Store the client ID and tenant ID in GitHub Secrets
Add the azure/login@v2 step to your workflow with OIDC parameters
Verify the workflow can run az account show successfully
data.expectedOutcome: A workflow that authenticates to Azure without storing a client secret.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use publish profiles for simple personal projects
Service principals with RBAC are better for team environments
OpenID Connect (OIDC) is the most secure option - no long-lived secrets
Always grant the minimum RBAC role needed for the deployment
data.takeaway: OIDC authentication removes the biggest security risk in CI/CD: long-lived secrets.
